summary: Configured node1 as the cluster NTP server and node2 to synchronize exclusively from node1. Both nodes remained correctly configured and healthy after sequential reboots.
actions_performed: Allowed 10.100.4.0/24 to query chronyd on node1 and enabled NTP in firewalld at runtime and permanently.
Disabled node2's public CentOS pool and DHCP-provided time sources; configured 10.100.4.10 as its sole source.
Verified active synchronization, normal tracking, NTP traffic, and zero packet drops.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.summary: node1 listens on UDP/123, permits the cluster subnet, has persistent firewall access, is synchronized upstream, and records node2 as an active client with no packet drops.

evidence.requirement: node2 synchronizes against node1 instead of public servers
evidence.summary: node2 has 10.100.4.10 as its sole configured and selected source; OS synchronization is yes, leap status is Normal, and waitsync succeeds.
Baseline boot ID 8f258838-e1de-494d-9d99-e5113b2865db, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 642f3798-8dbb-4f41-a2b8-a942bdce341f, recovered listener/service, and restored node2 synchronization.

Baseline boot ID be303eb3-eeb6-4466-86f1-fd6406dd7dad, reboot acknowledgement and outage, changed boot ID d3b5d8e7-96b1-4e3c-a85e-c52d49ccadfa, and recovered synchronization exclusively through node1.
